ordered_step_reconstruction: The Riesz operator T_rho on H_0^1 is bounded, positive, injective, self-adjoint and compact because the H_0^1 unit ball is relatively compact in L2 (indeed in C[0,1] in one dimension). Its positive compact spectral resolution yields the generalized min-max formula.
A sequence in K_R has a weak-star convergent subsequence because L1(0,1) is separable; the diagonal limit extends to an L1 functional and nonnegative tests preserve 1<=rho<=R.
For rho_j weak-star converging to rho, a fixed rho-spectral k-plane gives limsup lambda_k(rho_j)<=lambda_k(rho) because the denominator functionals converge uniformly on its compact unit sphere.

A moving rho_j-weighted-orthonormal first-k frame has uniform H_0^1 bounds. Weak H_0^1 and strong L2 limits preserve the weighted Gram matrix, hence preserve k independent directions; weak lower semicontinuity then gives lambda_k(rho)<=liminf lambda_k(rho_j).
The two inequalities give sequential weak-star continuity of lambda_n and lambda_{n+1}; applying it to maximizing and minimizing sequences gives both extrema.

ordered_step_reconstruction: For L-infinity positive rho, the shooting solution is W^{2,infinity}; the lifted Prüfer angle is absolutely continuous and satisfies theta_x=(s'^2+lambda rho s^2)/(s^2+s'^2)>0 a.e.

Differentiating the shooting integral equation in lambda gives (s' z-s z')'=rho s^2, so theta(1,lambda) is strictly increasing. Positivity of the first mode and the intermediate-value argument give exactly k-1 interior zeros for u_k.
On each u_n nodal cell, the strict comparison Wronskian identity forces at least one u_{n+1} zero; the exact nodal count forces exactly one and excludes a common interior zero.

With both left derivatives positive, u_n and u_{n+1} have the same sign before that zero and opposite signs after it. Hence W'=-(lambda_{n+1}-lambda_n)rho u_nu_{n+1} makes W decrease then increase on each cell.
At every interior u_n zero, -u_{n+1}u_n'<0. Together with W(0)=W(1)=0, this proves W<0 separately on the first, middle and last cells.

Thus q=u_{n+1}/u_n is strictly decreasing on each of n nodal cells. F_n=0 is exactly q=+sqrt(lambda_n/lambda_{n+1}) or q=-sqrt(lambda_n/lambda_{n+1}); each level is hit at most once per cell, yielding at most 2n zeros. At a hit q is nonzero and q'<0, so every zero is simple.

ordered_step_reconstruction: For arbitrary h in L-infinity, T_{rho+epsilon h}=T_rho+epsilon T_h in operator norm. Sturm simplicity isolates the kth compact-operator eigenvalue.

Normalized perturbed eigenvectors are precompact and converge to the oriented unperturbed eigenvector. Pairing the exact perturbed eigen-equation with that eigenvector gives mu_k'[h]=int h z_k^2 without assuming eigenvector differentiability.
Converting mu_k=1/lambda_k and z_k=u_k/sqrt(lambda_k) gives lambda_k'[h]=-lambda_k int h u_k^2, hence D_n'[h]=int h F_n.

At a maximizer, feasible positive directions localized on {rho<=R-delta} give F_n<=0 there, while feasible negative directions on {rho>=1+delta} give F_n>=0. Exhaustion over rational delta forces rho=R on {F_n>0} and rho=1 on {F_n<0}.

For a minimizer, the variational inequality reverses, yielding rho=1 on {F_n>0} and rho=R on {F_n<0}. The established finite zero set removes all positive-measure singular arcs, so every extremizer is bang-bang a.e. and any effective switch lies at an F_n zero.
